title: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth
subtitle: Two casts meet inside a labyrinth
summary: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth is Atlus' Nintendo 3DS dungeon role-playing crossover bringing together the casts of Persona 3 and Persona 4. They find themselves in an unfamiliar version of Yasogami High School with Zen and Rei, two young people who have lost their memories. body: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth is Atlus' Nintendo 3DS dungeon role-playing crossover bringing together the casts of Persona 3 and Persona 4. They find themselves in an unfamiliar version of Yasogami High School with Zen and Rei, two young people who have lost their memories. Escaping requires exploring the labyrinths connected to the school and recovering objects hidden within them. The familiar characters provide the conversations and party choices, while the first-person exploration draws on the map-making approach of Atlus' Etrian Odyssey series.

The upper screen presents corridors from the party's viewpoint, while the touchscreen holds a map that the player develops during exploration. Marking walls, passages and useful features turns progress through a maze into a record that can be consulted on the next visit. Battles use turn-based decisions and the abilities associated with Personas. Choosing a party therefore affects both its practical options and the characters sharing the expedition. Learning a dungeon means understanding its layout as well as preparing a group capable of surviving the encounters along the route.

Between expeditions, the school provides places to recover, sell collected materials, obtain equipment and work with Personas. These services connect discoveries inside the labyrinths with preparation for the next attempt. The crossover also creates space for conversations between characters who originally belonged to separate adventures. Their relationships develop around a shared immediate problem, rather than requiring the player to repeat the original stories. A return to the school offers a pause, a chance to adjust the team and another reason to take the assembled cast back into the maze.
